title: 1963 AHSME Problem 23
statement: \(A\) gives \(B\) as many cents as \(B\) has and \(C\) as many cents as \(C\) has. Similarly, \(B\) then gives \(A\) and \(C\) as many cents as each then has. \(C\), similarly, then gives \(A\) and \(B\) as many cents as each then has. If each finally has \(16\) cents, with how many cents does \(A\) start?

solutions.text:
Reverse the transactions. Before \(C\) gives, the holdings are \((8,8,32).\) Before \(B\) gives, they are \((4,28,16).\) Before \(A\) gives, \(B\) and \(C\) must have had \(14\) and \(8,\) while \(A\) had \(4+14+8=26.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Work backward from the final holdings
Immediately before someone gives, each recipient must have half of the amount held just after that gift
